blocks.text: The rear-wheel bearing of a delivery van must survive about 300 million wheel revolutions before it is replaced, and the catalogue number that tells the engineer whether it will is a single load rating $C$. Choosing a rolling bearing is a matter of comparing the load it will carry with that rating and turning the ratio into a life.

blocks.markdown: A rolling-element bearing carries load through balls or rollers that roll between an inner and an outer ring. Rolling contact has low friction, but the small contact areas produce very high local (Hertzian) stresses, and the surfaces eventually fail by **subsurface fatigue** (pitting or spalling), not by wear. The life is therefore a statistical quantity, which is why bearing life is quoted for a stated reliability.

blocks.title: Basic rating life and dynamic load rating
blocks.text: The basic rating life $L_{10}$ is the number of revolutions (in millions) that 90 per cent of a large group of identical bearings will complete or exceed before fatigue spalling appears. The basic dynamic load rating $C$ is the constant radial load that gives $L_{10}=1$ million revolutions. It is listed in manufacturers' catalogues, so the designer never needs to compute it.

blocks.caption: Rating life in millions of revolutions, with P the equivalent dynamic load in the same units as C, and in hours at speed n in rev/min

blocks.title: Life of a deep-groove ball bearing under radial load
blocks.prompt: A deep-groove ball bearing with dynamic load rating $C=30$ kN carries a steady radial load $P=5$ kN at 1450 rev/min. Find $L_{10}$ in millions of revolutions and in hours.

steps.text: Sensitivity: the life varies as the cube of the load, so a 10 per cent overload costs about 25 per cent of the life.

blocks.answer: $L_{10}=216$ million revolutions, which is about 2483 hours at 1450 rev/min.

blocks.markdown: **Equivalent dynamic load.** The rating $C$ is defined for a pure radial load. When a bearing carries both a radial load $F_r$ and an axial (thrust) load $F_a$, they are combined into an **equivalent dynamic load** $P$ that would give the same life as the combined loading. The radial and axial load factors $X$ and $Y$ come from the manufacturer's catalogue and depend on the type of bearing and on the ratio $F_a/F_r$. If the axial load is small, $F_a/(VF_r)\le e$ (where $e$ is a limit given in the catalogue), the axial load is ignored and $P=F_r$.

blocks.caption: Equivalent dynamic load; V = 1 when the inner ring rotates (1.2 when the outer ring rotates); X, Y and e from the catalogue

blocks.title: Combined radial and axial load
blocks.prompt: A deep-groove ball bearing with $C=22$ kN rotates at 1450 rev/min with its inner ring rotating ($V=1$). It carries $F_r=3.2$ kN and $F_a=1.4$ kN. The catalogue values for this ratio, taken here for illustration, are $X=0.56$ and $Y=1.6$. Find the equivalent load and $L_{10}$.

steps.text: The axial-to-radial ratio is 0.44, which is above the limit used here, so the axial load must be included.

blocks.answer: $P=4.03$ kN, $L_{10}=162$ million revolutions or about 1867 hours. The axial load raises the equivalent load by 26 per cent over the radial load alone.

rows: Wheel hubs, gearboxes with helical gears
Conveyors, fans with long shafts, heavy shock
Compact spaces, such as universal joints
blocks.caption: Rolling bearing types and the duties they suit (qualitative)

blocks.markdown: **Selecting a bearing type.** Selection starts with the direction of the load, the speed, the life required and the need for tolerance to misalignment. Ball bearings have point contact: low friction and high speed capability but lower load capacity. Roller bearings have line contact: greater capacity for a given size, at lower speed capability and less tolerance to misalignment. Tapered roller and angular-contact bearings carry combined loads but are fitted in pairs, with adjusted preload. Once a type is chosen, the required life gives the minimum $C$, which is used to select the size from the catalogue.

blocks.title: Required dynamic rating for a roller bearing
blocks.prompt: A cylindrical roller bearing carries a steady radial load of 9 kN at 600 rev/min and must achieve $L_{10h}=20000$ h. Find the minimum dynamic load rating $C$.

steps.text: Required life in millions of revolutions.
Invert the life equation with the roller exponent $a=10/3$, i.e. $C=PL_{10}^{1/a}=PL_{10}^{0.3}$.

blocks.answer: The bearing must have a basic dynamic load rating of at least 65 kN.

blocks.title: Ratings are for 90 per cent reliability
blocks.text: The basic rating life $L_{10}$ is the life that 90 per cent of bearings reach. Higher reliability needs a life adjustment factor less than 1 (supplied by the manufacturer), and shock loads, poor lubrication or contamination shorten the life well below $L_{10}$. Always allow for load factors for shock or vibration.

points: $L_{10}=(C/P)^a$ million revolutions, with $a=3$ for ball and $10/3$ for roller bearings; hours follow from $L_{10h}=10^6L_{10}/(60n)$.
The equivalent load for combined loading is $P=XVF_r+YF_a$ (or $VF_r$ when the axial load is small), with $X$, $Y$ and $e$ from the catalogue.
Life varies as the cube (ball) or the 10/3 power (roller) of the load, so a small overload costs a lot of life.
Select ball bearings for speed and light loads, roller bearings for heavy radial loads, tapered or angular-contact bearings for combined loads and spherical types for misalignment.

questions.stem: What does the basic rating life $L_{10}$ of a rolling bearing mean?

options.text: The life that 90 per cent of a group of identical bearings will reach or exceed under the same conditions
The life of the first bearing in the group to fail
The average life of the bearings
The life reached by 10 per cent of the bearings

questions.correctOptionText: The life that 90 per cent of a group of identical bearings will reach or exceed under the same conditions

distractorRationale.a: Correct: it is the 90 per cent reliability life.
distractorRationale.b: The earliest failure occurs well before L10.
distractorRationale.c: The average (median) life is about five times L10 for a typical bearing.
distractorRationale.d: 10 per cent fail by L10, not survive.

questions.explanation: Rolling bearing fatigue is statistical, so $L_{10}$ is quoted as the life at which 10 per cent have failed and 90 per cent are still running. The mean life is longer.

questions.stem: A ball bearing carries a load that is doubled while the speed stays the same. By what factor does its rating life change?

options.text: It falls to one eighth
It falls to one half
It falls to one quarter
It is unchanged

distractorRationale.a: Correct: L10 proportional to P^-3, so (1/2)^3 = 1/8.
distractorRationale.b: Half would need life inversely proportional to load.
distractorRationale.c: One quarter would need an exponent of 2.

questions.explanation: For ball bearings $L_{10}=(C/P)^3$, so doubling $P$ divides the life by $2^3=8$. This cubic dependence is why modest overloads shorten life significantly.

questions.stem: A cylindrical roller bearing carries a radial load that is halved. By approximately what factor does its rating life increase ($a=10/3$)?

options.text: About 10
About 8
About 2
About 4

distractorRationale.b: 8 would be the factor for a ball bearing (a = 3).
distractorRationale.c: 2 would apply if life were inversely proportional to load.
distractorRationale.d: 4 would result from an exponent of 2.

questions.explanation: With $L_{10}\propto P^{-10/3}$, halving the load multiplies the life by $2^{10/3}=10.1$. The roller exponent is slightly larger than the ball exponent, so roller bearing life is even more sensitive to load.

questions.stem: A shaft carrying a helical gear transmits a significant radial load and a significant axial thrust in one direction, with heavy loads and moderate speed. Which bearing arrangement is most appropriate?

options.text: A pair of tapered roller bearings mounted so that each takes thrust in one direction
A single cylindrical roller bearing at each end
A single deep-groove ball bearing carrying all the thrust
Needle roller bearings at both ends

questions.correctOptionText: A pair of tapered roller bearings mounted so that each takes thrust in one direction

distractorRationale.a: Correct: tapered rollers carry combined loads, and a pair locates the shaft axially.
distractorRationale.b: Cylindrical roller bearings carry radial load but not thrust.
distractorRationale.c: A deep-groove ball bearing has a limited axial capacity for heavy loads.
distractorRationale.d: Needle rollers carry radial load only.

questions.explanation: Tapered roller bearings have line contact on inclined races, so they carry heavy combined radial and axial loads. They are fitted in pairs so each takes thrust in one direction and sets the shaft position.

questions.stem: Why is the equivalent dynamic load $P$ used for combined radial and axial loading instead of simply using the radial load?

options.text: The rating $C$ is defined for a purely radial load, so the combined load must be converted into a single equivalent radial load that would give the same life
The axial load does not affect the life
The radial load is always smaller than the axial load
The equivalent load is always smaller than the radial load

questions.correctOptionText: The rating $C$ is defined for a purely radial load, so the combined load must be converted into a single equivalent radial load that would give the same life

distractorRationale.a: Correct: P puts the combined loading on the same footing as C.
distractorRationale.b: The axial load shortens the life when it is significant.
distractorRationale.c: There is no general relationship between the loads.
distractorRationale.d: P is generally larger than the radial load, not smaller.

questions.explanation: Catalogue ratings are for a pure radial load, so when thrust is present we use $P=XVF_r+YF_a$ to find the radial load that would damage the bearing equally. If the thrust is small compared with the radial load, $P=VF_r$ is enough.

questions.stem: A ball bearing has a dynamic load rating $C=35.8$ kN and carries an equivalent load $P=8$ kN. Find the basic rating life $L_{10}$ in millions of revolutions.
questions.explanation: The ratio is $C/P=35.8/8=4.475$, and for a ball bearing $a=3$, so $L_{10}=4.475^3=89.6$ million revolutions. This is the life that 90 per cent of such bearings reach.

questions.stem: A ball bearing with $C=40$ kN carries an equivalent load of 7.5 kN and runs at 750 rev/min. Find its basic rating life in hours.

A deep-groove ball bearing has an inner ring that rotates ($V=1$) and carries a radial load of 2.0 kN and an axial load of 3.0 kN. Because $F_a/F_r$ is large, the catalogue factors for this case are $X=0.45$ and $Y=1.2$ (illustrative values). Find the equivalent dynamic load in kN.
questions.explanation: Since the axial ratio exceeds the limit, $P=XVF_r+YF_a=0.45\times1\times2.0+1.2\times3.0=4.50$ kN. The axial load contributes four times as much as the radial one in this example.

questions.stem: Explain how the equivalent dynamic load is used with the dynamic load rating to estimate the life of a bearing that carries both radial and axial load, stating the equations, what $L_{10}$ means, and why the load exponent differs for ball and roller bearings.
markingGuide: The rating $C$ is for pure radial load; combined loads are converted to $P=XVF_r+YF_a$ (or $P=VF_r$ when $F_a/(VF_r)\le e$), with $X$, $Y$, $e$ from the catalogue and $V=1$ for a rotating inner ring.
$L_{10}$ is the life that 90 per cent of identical bearings reach or exceed (reliability 90 per cent).
Exponent $a=3$ for ball (point contact) and $10/3$ for roller (line contact), from the fitted relationship between load and fatigue life of the contact.
Small changes in load strongly alter the life, so shock factors and a margin on $P$ are used.
questions.explanation: The equivalent load is the radial load that would do the same fatigue damage as the real combination. The life then follows from the rating by a simple power law.

questions.stem: A vertical pump shaft is supported by two bearings: the lower one must carry a large axial hydraulic thrust and the upper one is to carry the radial load only and allow for thermal expansion of the shaft. The shaft turns at 1450 rev/min. Recommend suitable bearing types for the two positions and justify your choices, noting what you would do about misalignment and life.
markingGuide: Thrust position: a bearing able to carry large axial load, such as a thrust ball bearing, a pair of angular-contact ball bearings or a tapered roller pair, chosen for the thrust magnitude and speed.
Radial-only location (upper): a cylindrical roller bearing (or deep-groove ball bearing free to slide in its housing) that allows axial movement for thermal growth and carries only radial load.
One bearing locates the shaft axially (the thrust bearing) and the other floats, to avoid forcing the shaft into compression by thermal expansion.
Misalignment: use a self-aligning type or fit a flexible coupling if shaft deflection or housing misalignment is significant.
Life: compute the equivalent load for each bearing, and choose $C$ from $L_{10}=(C/P)^a$ to meet the required hours at 1450 rev/min with a margin for shock and contamination.
questions.explanation: The two bearings play different roles, so different types are appropriate. One must locate the shaft against the thrust and the other must be free to move along the shaft.
